<!-- ABOUTME: Records the observed shell wait lifetime defect behind card #623's process-fixture work. -->

# Card #623: shell wait lifetime

The historical PR #577 init failure reported the no-owner message instead of a timeout. Its process order is unknown. At the declared base `8fea50a`, a controlled run killed the stand-in's recorded tail after the shell wrote `ready`. The direct shell then ended at code 0 because its operand-free `wait` completed. L0 reported `timedOut=false`, and init printed the same no-owner message. That proves a reachable cause, not which ordering happened in PR #577.

The fixture now keeps its direct shell waiting after `wait` completes. In the same controlled tail-kill run, L0's timeout kills the shell, reports `timedOut=true`, and records the kill. The original timeout test still checks the text, empty process group, and kill records.

The PR #625 SIGINT failure's historical cause is likewise unproven. At this base, the cleanup command also ends in operand-free `wait`; controlled tail endings expose code-0 dispatch records through the Node child exit and process-table status routes. Keeping that command shell alive after its child ends makes cleanup's group kill produce a nonzero dispatch end. The tests record the selected status route and keep the original nonzero and ordering assertions.

The 2026-10-13 `npm test` run of this worktree, recorded as `c623-full-head-local.log`, passed 3,333 tests with 17 skips and no failures. Its start/end one-minute loads were 8.32/11.58 on 12 logical CPUs. The targeted `c623-affected-complete.log` run passed all 285 tests in the four affected files.

This fix changes test fixtures. It does not change L0's status classification or claim that a tail's exit status is the shell's exit status. In the 2026-10-13 `npm test` run recorded as `c623-cells-base-first.log` at `8fea50a`, each of the 20 C2/C3 D0–D3 and reachable R0a/R0b/R1 forcings ended the direct shell at code 0 and printed the no-owner message. The child statuses were 0, 1, 137 from the test's SIGKILL, and 127 from failed exec. The three C1-D4 controls and 12 C4 controls each reported timeout at that base in `c623-controls-base.log`; the three C6 controls reported no owner. The corrected C7 control's direct shell exited 7 in `c623-c7-control-base.log`. The historical PR #577 ordering remains unproven because no unforced run reproduced it.

For the in-group D4 case, C5's tail-only group kill is excluded by the final-base call path: `src/substrate/process.mjs` sends SIGKILL to the negative group id, and a shell still blocked in bare `wait` on a live tail remains a member of that group. A trace showing both alive in the group immediately before that signal, followed by the tail receiving it while the shell does not, would falsify this exclusion.

## Full runner outputs

The log name identifies each run. Each block is the complete output captured when that run ended, including the start/end host readings where the runner recorded them. Intentionally red final-base tests remain red here; their passing-head counterparts are separate blocks. Literal trailing spaces are displayed as `␠`, one symbol per space, so the repository whitespace check can read the output without changing its content.
